steps.title: Let us run a sample shop
steps.instruction: We will add a steel water bottle, record 24 bottles in stock, then sell two for INR 250 each.
steps.note: The example uses made-up details. You can pause the video or repeat any chapter.

steps.title: Create your account
steps.instruction: Choose Set up my business, then a sign-in option. After sign-in, enter your business name and workspace address.
steps.note: Already have an account? Choose Sign in instead. Your workspace is your business area in Tenali.

steps.title: Add your shop details
steps.instruction: In Company Setup, enter your business name, address, phone and email. Display Name is the name customers see.
steps.note: Storefront Address is the short part of your shop link. Check spelling and choose Save Changes when finished.

steps.title: What does this GST switch do?
steps.instruction: Off: sales documents have no GST. On: GST applies and GSTIN is needed. This sample shop is not GST-registered, so we use Off.
steps.note: For a GST-registered business, turn it on and enter the registered GSTIN. The switch changes documents; it does not register your business for GST.

steps.title: Find your way around
steps.instruction: Open the three-line menu. Product Inventory is for items, Billing is for sales bills, and Dashboard is for a quick business check.
steps.note: On a smaller screen, open the three-line menu first. The guide names the buttons as they appear in the app.

steps.title: Add your first product
steps.instruction: Open Product Inventory, then choose Add Product. A product is one of the things you sell.
steps.note: Start with one item. You can use Bulk Excel later for a longer list.

steps.title: Give the item a clear name
steps.instruction: Product Name: Steel water bottle. SKU: BOTTLE-01. SKU is your own short item code. Use a name you will recognise.
steps.note: Use a name you will recognise when making a bill. Avoid creating the same item twice.

steps.title: Group similar products
steps.instruction: Choose or type the brand and category. HSN / SAC groups products for tax. Select a matching saved code when needed.
steps.note: Saved HSN choices show their description and GST rate. This example still has GST off for sales.

steps.title: Set the selling price
steps.instruction: Choose Keep catalog price. Enter 250 in Catalog Price (INR). This is the catalogue selling price, not your supplier's buying price.
steps.note: Buying price is what you pay a supplier. It is not the price you charge a customer.

steps.title: Add a product picture
steps.instruction: Choose a Product Image file, or enter its image URL. Check the preview. Use PNG, JPEG or WebP under 1 MB.
steps.note: For a single-product upload, use a PNG, JPEG or WebP under 1 MB. The image shown here is a sample illustration.

steps.title: Save and check the product
steps.instruction: Keep Active selected. Review the details, then choose Save Product. Adding a product does not add physical stock; that comes next.
steps.note: Saving a product does not add physical stock. We will enter the bottles already in the shop next.

steps.title: Enter your opening stock
steps.instruction: Owned Stock: select your store and Stock In. Quantity: 24. Reason: Opening stock. Choose Record Stock Movement once.
steps.note: Opening stock means items you already have when you start. Enter it once; do not enter a purchase again if its stock was already recorded.

steps.title: Add many products with Excel
steps.instruction: Choose Bulk Excel, then Products and Download products template. Fill the Data sheet in Excel. The README sheet explains each column.
steps.note: The README sheet explains the columns. Use the template instead of starting with an empty sheet.

steps.title: Include photos in a bulk file
steps.instruction: Web pictures: use public HTTPS links in image_url. Local files: use image_file filenames, then ZIP manifest.xlsx with its images folder.
steps.note: Local files go in a ZIP: manifest.xlsx plus an images folder containing those files. Use the matching filename for each product.

steps.title: Check what the upload saved
steps.instruction: Choose your file, then Upload & process. Download results: success.xlsx lists saved rows; failure.xlsx explains errors. Fix only failed rows. Resume an interrupted import rather than starting again.
steps.note: success.xlsx lists saved rows; failure.xlsx explains rows to fix. Retry only failed rows. If interrupted, resume the saved import rather than uploading everything again.

steps.title: Choose the customer
steps.instruction: Open Billing. Choose Sales invoice and the billing store. Find your customer, or choose Add customer here to enter a new one.
steps.note: For a new customer, choose Add customer here, enter their details and save. This example uses Sample customer.

steps.title: Check the bill details
steps.instruction: Set the invoice date and Bill To Address. Place of Supply is the sale's state. Keep Ship to billing address checked for the same delivery address.
steps.note: Place of Supply is the state used for this sale. Enter the correct customer and delivery details before continuing.

steps.title: Add the items being sold
steps.instruction: Select Steel water bottle from Product / Inventory. Quantity: 2. Price: 250. Use Add Item for another product on the same bill.
steps.note: Quantity means how many units the customer is buying, not how much stock you have.

steps.title: Check the total
steps.instruction: Check the total: 2 bottles x INR 250 = INR 500. This sample shop has no GST. Check your own bill's tax too.
steps.note: This example has no GST because the sample shop is not GST-registered. A quotation is only an offer and does not change stock.

steps.title: Record money received
steps.instruction: The customer pays INR 300. Enter Amount Received Now: 300, Payment Mode: cash, and Received In Account: Shop cash. INR 200 remains due.
steps.note: INR 500 minus INR 300 leaves INR 200 still due. Do not enter the full total if only part was paid.

steps.title: Post the invoice once
steps.instruction: Keep Auto-create receivable for unpaid balance checked: this tracks the INR 200 still owed. Review the bill, choose Post Invoice once, and wait for confirmation.
steps.note: Do not repeat a save because it feels slow. Check the result first. Posting this sale records two bottles sold and leaves INR 200 to collect.

steps.title: Check what is left
steps.instruction: Open the bottle's Owned Stock tab. 24 bottles minus 2 sold leaves 22. Check Stock History; do not enter the same sale again manually.
steps.note: Check the store breakdown and Stock History. Do not also enter a manual Stock Out for the same posted sale.

steps.title: Check money still due
steps.instruction: Open Dashboard and choose the reporting period. Collections shows money customers still owe: INR 200 in our example. Older unpaid bills can appear here too.
steps.note: Outstanding collections can include older unpaid bills, not only the selected month. Record a later payment against the existing due amount, not as another sale.

steps.title: Choose what customers can see
steps.instruction: The online shop is optional. In Edit Product, check photos and price, then select Visible in customer catalog and save.
steps.note: Keep unfinished items hidden until their details are ready. Active and catalogue visibility are separate settings.

steps.title: Prepare your shop page
steps.instruction: In Company Setup, check Storefront Address and Storefront open to the public. Choose Save Changes. Storefront Design changes colours, pictures and layout.
steps.note: If the public-shop switch is disabled, the platform has not enabled that feature for this workspace. The rest of your shop work can continue.

steps.title: Check the customer view
steps.instruction: Open Customer View. Check the picture, name and price as a customer would. Your storefront is your online shop. Share its link when ready.
steps.note: A storefront is the customer-facing online shop. Your operations menu remains for you and your team.

steps.title: Ask a question in your words
steps.instruction: When AI is enabled, open Tenali AI and choose New chat. Type your question in everyday words. This example does not send an AI request.
steps.note: You can describe the task in everyday language. This guide shows the question, not a live AI answer.

steps.title: Use documents and review the result
steps.instruction: Attach a bill or catalogue using the paperclip. For products, select Prepare product bulk workbook first. Check AI suggestions before saving business records.
steps.note: AI suggestions are a starting point. Check names, quantities, prices and tax. You stay in control of what becomes a business record.
